nodes.label: Task Residual Spectrum (TRS)
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: TRS = departure of LoRA B-matrix singular values from the Marchenko-Pastur null distribution. Architecture-agnostic (GL_r-invariant), task-specific, sqrt(N)-bounded by NTK theory. Proposed as universal task fingerprint. Canonical form via QR+SVD resolves factorization ambiguity.

nodes.label: Marchenko-Pastur Distribution
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: RMT null distribution for random matrices, depends only on aspect ratio d_out/r. Singular values conforming to MP = noise; departing = learned task signal. Used as baseline for TRS computation.

nodes.label: GL_r Invariance of LoRA B-matrix
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Singular values of B matrix invariant under GL_r group action (B -> BM for invertible M). Three independent proofs: algebraic (SymmetriesInWSL), Riemannian geometry (Frechet arXiv:2604.27155), ML (LoL arXiv:2410.04207). Mathematically necessary for principled LoRA comparison.

nodes.label: Intruder Dimensions
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: LoRA B-matrix singular directions that are novel relative to the base model pretrained weight directions. God node with degree 13 in the existing knowledge graph. High TRS = high intruder dimension content.

nodes.label: Fisher Subspace
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Fisher information matrices guide LoRA initialization into high-curvature subspaces. Approximately shared across architectures under Platonic hypothesis. Fisher-initialized LoRAs predicted to have more similar TRS across models.

nodes.label: Spectral Over-Accumulation (SVC)
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: During LoRA merging, task identity resides in distinct singular directions. Shared singular directions over-accumulate, causing interference. SVC = singular value calibration using empirical shared distribution as null.

nodes.label: 2D Layer Selection Map (alpha x TRS)
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Novel layer selection criterion combining AlphaLoRA's PL_Alpha_Hill (alpha) with TRS. Four quadrants: gold (high alpha + high TRS), dormant (high alpha + low TRS), rescued (low alpha + high TRS), noise (low alpha + low TRS).

nodes.label: Bayesian Spectral Calibration
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Unified Bayesian framework where TRS (MP null) and SVC (empirical shared distribution) are special cases of a prior over singular value distributions. Spiked RMT establishes TRS as optimal Bayes estimator of task signal via Gauss-Markov theorem.

nodes.label: Spiked Random Matrix Theory
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Spiked RMT model: signal matrix plus noise matrix. Establishes theoretical optimality of TRS as Bayes estimator of task signal. BBP transition identifies rank of true signal.

nodes.label: NTK Optimal Rank Bound sqrt(N)
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: NTK theory implies optimal LoRA rank = sqrt(N) where N is dataset size. Architecture-independent, dataset-dependent bound. Provides upper bound on number of meaningful TRS dimensions.

nodes.label: Grokking as Spectral Phase Transition
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Grokking (delayed generalization) corresponds to a phase transition where effective rank of LoRA B matrix drops. Post-grokking B matrix encodes task's intrinsic geometry in its surviving singular directions.

nodes.label: Universal Weight Subspace Hypothesis
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: 1100+ models converge to shared spectral subspaces within architectures. Open question: do cross-architecture universal subspaces align? Connects to Platonic Representation Hypothesis.

nodes.label: Subspace Geometry and Catastrophic Forgetting
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Minimum principal angle between task gradient subspaces governs catastrophic forgetting during sequential fine-tuning. TRS distance approximates this principal angle without explicit gradient computation.

nodes.label: LoL Paradigm (Learning on LoRAs)
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Meta-network trained on LoRA weights to predict task properties (e.g., task identity, performance). GL_r symmetry handled via canonicalization equivalent to QR+SVD decomposition. Enables learning directly on LoRA weight space.

nodes.label: Canonical TRS via QR+SVD
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Resolves LoRA factorization ambiguity: QR decompose B, then SVD of R, then TRS = log(sigma_i / lambda_MP_edge). Produces unique canonical representation invariant to GL_r transformations.

nodes.label: Task Arithmetic Kernel
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Kernel function on task pairs defined via TRS inner product. Enables geometric task arithmetic: task addition, subtraction, interpolation in TRS space. Connects to kernel methods for structured prediction.

nodes.label: Rank-Normalized Spectral Embedding
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Embedding LoRAs in a normalized spectral space using TRS values padded to fixed length. Enables comparison across different ranks and architectures via cosine similarity.

nodes.label: LoRA Generative Modeling
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Diffusion or flow model in LoRA weight space conditioned on TRS. Can generate new LoRAs for unseen tasks by sampling from learned distribution of TRS-conditioned weights.

nodes.label: TDA on LoRA Populations
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Topological Data Analysis applied to populations of LoRA TRS vectors. Persistent homology reveals topological structure of task space. Betti numbers encode task diversity and relationships.

nodes.label: AlphaLoRA: Rank Allocation via HT-SR
nodes.author: Qing, Gao, Zhou, Diao, Yang, Vosoughi

nodes.label: PL_Alpha_Hill Metric
nodes.author: Qing, Gao, Zhou, Diao, Yang, Vosoughi
nodes.rationale: PL_Alpha_Hill = 1 + k / (sum_{i=1}^k ln(lambda_{n-i+1}/lambda_{n-k})). Hill estimator for power-law exponent alpha of ESD tail. Measures training quality of each layer. Lower alpha = heavier tail = better trained.

nodes.label: AlphaLoRA Rank Allocation Formula
nodes.author: Qing, Gao, Zhou, Diao, Yang, Vosoughi
nodes.rationale: s_i = floor((v_i^beta / sum(v_j^beta)) * T). Allocates total rank budget T across layers proportional to normalized alpha values raised to power beta. Outperforms MoLA baseline with 50% fewer parameters.

nodes.label: Stable Rank Metric
nodes.author: Qing, Gao, Zhou, Diao, Yang, Vosoughi
nodes.rationale: Stable_Rank = ||W||_F^2 / ||W||_2^2. Ratio of Frobenius norm squared to spectral norm squared. Soft rank measure robust to small singular values. Used as alternative to integer rank in HT-SR analysis.

nodes.label: Alpha_Hat Metric
nodes.author: Qing, Gao, Zhou, Diao, Yang, Vosoughi
nodes.rationale: Alpha_Hat = alpha * log(lambda_max). Combines power-law exponent with scale of largest eigenvalue. Used as alternative to PL_Alpha_Hill; includes absolute scale information.

nodes.label: Empirical Spectral Density (ESD)
nodes.author: Qing, Gao, Zhou, Diao, Yang, Vosoughi
nodes.rationale: ESD = distribution of eigenvalues of A = W^T W. Foundation for HT-SR analysis. Well-trained layers exhibit heavy-tailed ESD; poorly trained layers show bulk (Marchenko-Pastur) ESD.

nodes.label: Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization (HT-SR) Theory
nodes.author: Martin and Mahoney 2019-2021
nodes.rationale: Well-trained deep network layers exhibit heavy-tailed ESD. Power-law exponent alpha measures implicit regularization quality. HT-SR metrics (PL_Alpha_Hill, Alpha_Hat, Stable_Rank) predict generalization without test data.

nodes.label: LoRA-MoE Architecture
nodes.author: Qing, Gao, Zhou, Diao, Yang, Vosoughi
nodes.rationale: Multiple LoRA experts per layer with Mixture-of-Experts routing. AlphaLoRA allocates experts (ranks) by HT-SR metrics. Outperforms MoLA with fewer total parameters.

nodes.label: AlphaLoRA Experiments
nodes.author: Qing, Gao, Zhou, Diao, Yang, Vosoughi
nodes.rationale: Models: LLaMA-7B, LLaMA-2-7B, Mistral-7B. Tasks: MRPC, CoLA, RTE, ScienceQA, CommonsenseQA, OpenBookQA, GSM8K, SVAMP, AddSub, MultiArith. AlphaLoRA consistently outperforms uniform rank allocation and MoLA baseline.

nodes.label: Cross-LoRA Framework
nodes.author: Xia et al.
nodes.rationale: Data-free, training-free framework for transferring LoRA adapters across heterogeneous LLM architectures. Two-stage: LoRA-Align (subspace alignment) + LoRA-Shift (weight projection). Enables reuse of LoRAs across model families.

nodes.label: LoRA-Align Component
nodes.author: Xia et al.
nodes.rationale: Rank-truncated SVD + Frobenius-optimal linear transform. P_hat_U = argmin_P ||PU_s - U_t||_F^2; U_tilde_s = P_hat_U * U_s. Aligns source LoRA singular subspace to target model's weight subspace.

nodes.label: LoRA-Shift Component
nodes.author: Xia et al.
nodes.rationale: Frobenius projection into target subspace. Delta_W_t = U_tilde_s (U_tilde_s^T Delta_W_s V_tilde_s) V_tilde_s^T. Projects aligned source LoRA weights onto target model's principal subspace.

nodes.label: Rank-320 Truncation Strategy
nodes.author: Xia et al.
nodes.rationale: Rank-320 truncation retains >= 99% Frobenius energy. Reduces SVD complexity from O(mn*min(m,n)) to O(rmn). Approximately 20 minutes on 8GB GPU for full model transfer.

nodes.label: Architecture Sensitivity in Cross-LoRA
nodes.author: Xia et al.
nodes.rationale: GQA+SwiGLU+RMSNorm models (LLaMA, Qwen) transfer well to each other. MHA+GeLU architecture (Gemma-2-2B) shows inconsistent transfer. Architecture similarity predicts transfer success.

nodes.label: Cross-LoRA Transfer Experiments
nodes.author: Xia et al.
nodes.rationale: Models: LLaMA-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B, Gemma-2-2B. Results: up to +5.26% on ARC-c, +3.32% on ARC-e over zero-shot baseline. Data-free and training-free.

nodes.label: Model Merging via Task Vectors
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Task vectors = fine-tuned weights minus pretrained weights. Arithmetic operations (add, subtract, negate) on task vectors produce meaningful model behaviors. Spectral over-accumulation occurs when merging vectors with shared singular directions.

nodes.label: LoRA as Subspace Projection
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: LoRA constrains weight updates to low-rank subspace: Delta_W = BA where B in R^{d_out x r}, A in R^{r x d_in}. Factorization is non-unique (GL_r ambiguity). Singular values of B encode task-specific signal.

nodes.label: Platonic Representation Hypothesis
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Large neural networks converge to similar internal representations regardless of architecture or modality. Implies Fisher matrices and weight subspaces are approximately shared. Supports cross-architecture LoRA transfer feasibility.

nodes.label: Weight Space Learning (SymmetriesInWSL)
nodes.source_location: Paper: Symmetries in Weight Space Learning
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Algebraic proof that LoRA weight space has GL_r symmetry. Networks with the same function but different parameterizations are equivalent. Canonicalization required for learning on weights.

nodes.label: Frechet Mean in Riemannian LoRA Space
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Riemannian geometry proof that singular values of B are invariant under GL_r (Frechet mean argument). Provides metric on LoRA weight space where GL_r orbits are identified.
nodes.norm_label: frechet mean in riemannian lora space

nodes.label: Cross-Architecture Model Comparison
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Comparing LoRA adapters trained on different architectures. TRS provides architecture-agnostic fingerprint enabling such comparison. Cross-LoRA paper provides empirical validation of cross-architecture transfer.

nodes.label: Task Identity via Spectral Analysis
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Task identity is encoded in the singular value spectrum of LoRA B matrices. Two LoRAs trained on the same task (different seeds, architectures) should have similar TRS. Empirical test: 3 models x 10 tasks x 5 seeds = 150 LoRAs.

nodes.label: LoRA Rank and Effective Rank Analysis
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Effective rank of learned LoRA B matrices often much less than nominal rank r. Effective rank relates to number of task-specific signal dimensions. sqrt(N) NTK bound provides theoretical upper limit.
nodes.norm_label: lora rank and effective rank analysis

nodes.label: Spectral Geometry of Task Space
nodes.author: barsatKhadka
nodes.rationale: Task space has geometric structure revealed by TRS vectors. Distances in TRS space correspond to semantic task similarity. Principal angles between B-matrix column spaces measure task overlap.

nodes.label: Fréchet Mean on Riemannian Manifold
nodes.author: Marvin F. da Silva, Mohammed Adnan, Felix Dangel, Sageev Oore
nodes.rationale: Central concept: the paper reframes model merging as finding the Fréchet mean (generalised barycenter) on a Riemannian manifold equipped with a geodesic distance, enabling principled geometry-aware averaging of model weights.

nodes.label: Quotient Manifold / GL(r) Symmetry in LoRA Factorizations
nodes.author: Marvin F. da Silva, Mohammed Adnan, Felix Dangel, Sageev Oore
nodes.rationale: LoRA weight increments ΔW = GH have an inherent GL(r) symmetry: (G, H) ~ (GA^{-1}, HA^T) for invertible A. This makes the LoRA parameter space a quotient manifold, and orbit alignment (gauge fixing) is needed before averaging.
nodes.norm_label: quotient manifold / gl(r) symmetry in lora factorizations

nodes.label: Orbit Alignment / Gauge Fixing for LoRA Merging
nodes.author: Marvin F. da Silva, Mohammed Adnan, Felix Dangel, Sageev Oore
nodes.rationale: Before merging LoRA adapters, parameters from different orbits must be aligned to a canonical representative (gauge). Without this, averaging is ambiguous. GeoMerge uses polar decomposition (ΔW = UBV^T) to fix to O(r) gauge.
nodes.norm_label: orbit alignment / gauge fixing for lora merging

nodes.label: Polar Factorization / O(r) Symmetry (ΔW = UBV^T)
nodes.author: Marvin F. da Silva, Mohammed Adnan, Felix Dangel, Sageev Oore
nodes.rationale: Factorizing ΔW = UBV^T (polar form) reduces the GL(r) symmetry to O(r) symmetry. U and V lie on the Stiefel manifold; B is SPD. This enables separate Riemannian averaging on each factor.

nodes.label: Stiefel Manifold and SPD Manifold (Affine-Invariant Metric)
nodes.author: Marvin F. da Silva, Mohammed Adnan, Felix Dangel, Sageev Oore
nodes.rationale: GeoMerge averages U and V on the Stiefel manifold using canonical metric, and B on the SPD manifold using the affine-invariant metric. These are Riemannian manifolds with well-defined geodesics and Fréchet means.
nodes.norm_label: stiefel manifold and spd manifold (affine-invariant metric)

nodes.label: Fisher-Rao Geodesic Distance and Fisher Information Matrix
nodes.author: Marvin F. da Silva, Mohammed Adnan, Felix Dangel, Sageev Oore
nodes.rationale: The Fisher-Rao metric induces a Riemannian geometry on the parameter space via the Fisher Information Matrix. The Fréchet mean under this metric is intractable in general, but Fisher merging provides a tractable quadratic surrogate (Mahalanobis approximation).
nodes.norm_label: fisher-rao geodesic distance and fisher information matrix

nodes.label: Fisher Merging as Tractable Mahalanobis/Fréchet Surrogate
nodes.author: Marvin F. da Silva, Mohammed Adnan, Felix Dangel, Sageev Oore
nodes.rationale: Fisher merging (inverse-Fisher-weighted parameter average) is shown to be the solution to a quadratic approximation of the Fréchet mean under Fisher-Rao metric, making it geometrically interpretable as an approximate Fréchet mean.
nodes.norm_label: fisher merging as tractable mahalanobis/frechet surrogate

nodes.label: GeoMerge Algorithm (Riemannian/Quotient Merging of LoRA Adapters)
nodes.author: Marvin F. da Silva, Mohammed Adnan, Felix Dangel, Sageev Oore
nodes.rationale: GeoMerge: (1) align LoRA orbits via polar decomposition, (2) separate into Stiefel (U,V) and SPD (B) factors, (3) compute Riemannian Fréchet means on each manifold, (4) reconstruct merged adapter. Outperforms KnOTS on Llama-3 8B NLI tasks at 1/6 rank.
nodes.norm_label: geomerge algorithm (riemannian/quotient merging of lora adapters)

nodes.label: Fisher Energy E(Z) for LoRA Direction Selection
nodes.author: Zhi-Quan Feng, Ying-Jia Lin, Hung-Yu Kao
nodes.rationale: FILet defines Fisher Energy E(Z) = vec(Z)^T S_W vec(Z) for a LoRA direction Z, where S_W is the Fisher information of the pretrained weights W_0. Directions with minimal Fisher Energy cause least disruption to pretrained knowledge, making them ideal for LoRA initialization.
nodes.norm_label: fisher energy e(z) for lora direction selection

nodes.label: K-FAC Kronecker-Factored Fisher Approximation (S_W ≈ S_X ⊗ S_Y)
nodes.author: Zhi-Quan Feng, Ying-Jia Lin, Hung-Yu Kao
nodes.rationale: The full Fisher S_W is intractable to compute and invert. K-FAC approximates it as a Kronecker product S_W ≈ S_X ⊗ S_Y, where S_X and S_Y are computed from input activations and gradient covariances. This factorization makes the Fisher Energy tractable.
nodes.norm_label: k-fac kronecker-factored fisher approximation (s_w ≈ s_x ⊗ s_y)

nodes.label: FILet Algorithm (Fisher-Guided LoRA Initialization via Minimum Fisher Energy)
nodes.author: Zhi-Quan Feng, Ying-Jia Lin, Hung-Yu Kao
nodes.rationale: FILet: (1) compute S_X and S_Y via K-FAC from minibatch, (2) project Fisher into surrogate basis V̂=normalize(G_X), Û=normalize(W_0 V̂), (3) select top-r directions by minimum Fisher Energy (TopK(-Σ_fisher, r)), (4) initialize LoRA A and B from selected directions. Outperforms PiSSA, MiLoRA, KaSA, LoRA-Dash.
nodes.norm_label: filet algorithm (fisher-guided lora initialization via minimum fisher energy)

nodes.label: LoRA Subspace Initialization (Structured vs Random Initialization)
nodes.author: Zhi-Quan Feng, Ying-Jia Lin, Hung-Yu Kao
nodes.rationale: The choice of which subspace LoRA adapts determines both training efficiency and interference with pretrained knowledge. FILet, PiSSA, MiLoRA, and KaSA are all subspace initialization strategies; FILet selects minimal-disturbance directions via Fisher Energy.
nodes.norm_label: lora subspace initialization (structured vs random initialization)

nodes.label: Effective Dimensionality D (FSS Exponent: s_max ~ N^D)
nodes.author: Ping Wang
nodes.rationale: D is extracted from finite-size scaling: the maximum gradient avalanche size s_max scales as N^D across 8 model sizes (N=81 to 2001). D<1 is sub-diffusive (pre-grokking), D≈1 is critical (transition), D>1 is super-diffusive (post-grokking). This quantifies the geometry of gradient flow.
nodes.norm_label: effective dimensionality d (fss exponent: s_max ~ n^d)

nodes.label: Sub-Diffusive Gradient Regime (D < 1, Pre-Grokking)
nodes.author: Ping Wang
nodes.rationale: Before grokking, D≈0.90 indicating sub-diffusive gradient dynamics: gradient updates are locally confined, memorization is maintained, and generalization has not emerged. The gradient field lacks long-range correlations.

nodes.label: Super-Diffusive Gradient Regime (D > 1, Post-Grokking)
nodes.author: Ping Wang
nodes.rationale: After grokking, D≈1.20 indicating super-diffusive gradient dynamics: gradient updates propagate globally, indicating the model has found an organized generalizing solution. Long-range gradient correlations signal the discovery of hidden structure.

nodes.label: Self-Organized Criticality (SOC) at Grokking Transition
nodes.author: Ping Wang
nodes.rationale: The grokking transition exhibits SOC: gradient avalanches follow power-law distributions (characteristic of criticality), D passes through 1 (the SOC critical point), and the system self-organizes to the phase boundary without external tuning.

nodes.label: TDU-OFC Threshold-Based Diffusion Update Probe
nodes.author: Ping Wang
nodes.rationale: TDU-OFC is an Olami-Feder-Christensen cellular automaton adapted to monitor gradient dynamics. Updates fire when gradient |∇L| exceeds threshold τ=Q90(|∇L|), with diffusion strength α=0.3. Avalanche size statistics across model sizes yield the D exponent via FSS.

nodes.label: Weight Concentration (Gini Coefficient) Peak at Generalization Transition
nodes.author: Ping Wang
nodes.rationale: The Gini coefficient of weight magnitudes peaks ~+25% at the grokking transition, indicating that weight mass concentrates into a sparse generalizing structure at the critical point, consistent with algorithmic simplification of the solution.
nodes.norm_label: weight concentration (gini coefficient) peak at generalization transition

nodes.label: Grokking as Dimensional Phase Transition (D crosses 1 at critical point)
nodes.author: Ping Wang
nodes.rationale: The paper's central claim: grokking is a phase transition in gradient field geometry, measurable by effective dimensionality D extracted from FSS. D~0.90 (pre), D~1.0 (critical), D~1.20 (post) with R^2>0.99 fit, aggregate γ≈1.15 across 8 model scales.
nodes.norm_label: grokking as dimensional phase transition (d crosses 1 at critical point)

nodes.label: HTSR Power-Law Exponent α (Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization)
nodes.author: Hari K. Prakash, Charles H. Martin
nodes.rationale: HTSR theory: the ESD (Empirical Spectral Density) of weight matrices follows a heavy-tailed power law P(λ)~λ^{-α}. α≈2 is the optimal generalization regime; α<2 indicates overfitting or anti-grokking; α>2 indicates memorization. α is a diagnostic for model quality without labels.

nodes.label: Anti-Grokking: Late-Stage Generalization Collapse (α < 2 after 10^7 steps)
nodes.author: Hari K. Prakash, Charles H. Martin
nodes.rationale: Anti-grokking is a novel phenomenon identified in this paper: after the grokking generalization peak, continued training past ~10^7 steps causes validation accuracy to collapse. α drops below 2 (reaching ~1.1), correlation traps appear, and the model returns to an overfitting-like regime.
nodes.norm_label: anti-grokking: late-stage generalization collapse (α < 2 after 10^7 steps)

nodes.label: Correlation Traps (Anomalous Eigenvalues in W^rand ESD)
nodes.author: Hari K. Prakash, Charles H. Martin
nodes.rationale: Correlation traps are anomalous eigenvalues λ_trap >> λ^+_rand (Marchenko-Pastur upper edge) detected in the ESD of randomized W^rand. Their presence indicates that correlations have become pathologically dominant, signaling anti-grokking. KS test confirms deviation from MP (p≈1.877×10^{-5}, 9 traps detected).
nodes.norm_label: correlation traps (anomalous eigenvalues in w^rand esd)

nodes.label: Empirical Spectral Density (ESD) and Marchenko-Pastur Distribution
nodes.author: Hari K. Prakash, Charles H. Martin
nodes.rationale: The ESD of weight matrices is compared to the Marchenko-Pastur (MP) distribution (expected for random Gaussian matrices) to detect meaningful structure. Deviations from MP indicate heavy-tailed self-regularization; α is fit from the tail of the ESD.
nodes.norm_label: empirical spectral density (esd) and marchenko-pastur distribution

nodes.label: Three HTSR Phases of Grokking (Pre-Grokking α≈5, Grokking α≈2, Anti-Grokking α<2)
nodes.author: Hari K. Prakash, Charles H. Martin
nodes.rationale: The paper identifies three HTSR phases: (1) pre-grokking: α≈5 (strongly heavy-tailed, memorization), (2) grokking: α≈2.9→2 (transitional, optimal generalization), (3) anti-grokking: α<2≈1.1 (extreme heavy tails, correlation traps, generalization collapse). This extends grokking phenomenology to include late-stage failure.
nodes.norm_label: three htsr phases of grokking (pre-grokking α≈5, grokking α≈2, anti-grokking α<2)

nodes.label: Local Learning Coefficient (LLC): Diffeomorphism-Invariant Effective Complexity
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: The LLC (Local Learning Coefficient) is an SLT quantity that measures the effective complexity of a parameter basin. It is diffeomorphism-invariant and quantifies how many effective parameters the loss landscape exploits near a solution. Low LLC = simpler, more generalising solution.
nodes.norm_label: local learning coefficient (llc): diffeomorphism-invariant effective complexity

nodes.label: Memorisation Basin (High-LLC, Poor Generalisation)
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: The memorisation basin is a loss basin reached early in training with high LLC (many effective parameters), encoding data by lookup. It has near-zero training loss but high validation loss. During grokking, the model transitions away from this basin.

nodes.label: Generalisation Basin (Low-LLC, Structured Algorithmic Solution)
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: The generalisation basin has low LLC (few effective parameters), encoding the task via an elegant algorithmic structure (e.g., Fourier features for modular arithmetic). The model transitions to this basin during grokking, reducing its effective complexity.

nodes.label: SLT Local Free Energy / Bayesian Free Energy (RLCT-based)
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: SLT shows that the Bayesian free energy F(n) = nL_n + λ log n - (m-1) log log n, where λ is the RLCT (which equals LLC). The basin with lower free energy dominates at large n, providing a thermodynamic explanation for the grokking phase transition.
nodes.norm_label: slt local free energy / bayesian free energy (rlct-based)

nodes.label: Grokking as Bayesian Phase Transition between Competing Basins
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: The SLT framework explains grokking as a Bayesian phase transition: as training data n increases, the generalisation basin eventually dominates in Bayesian free energy over the memorisation basin, causing the abrupt accuracy jump. LLC trajectories computed from training data mirror validation loss dynamics.
nodes.norm_label: grokking as bayesian phase transition between competing basins

nodes.label: Singular Learning Theory (SLT, Watanabe) and RLCT
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: SLT (Watanabe 2009) extends Bayesian theory to singular statistical models (e.g., neural networks) where the Fisher information is degenerate. The RLCT (Real Log-Canonical Threshold) replaces the number of parameters as the effective complexity measure. LLC is the local version of RLCT estimated near a training solution.
nodes.norm_label: singular learning theory (slt, watanabe) and rlct

nodes.label: Grokking Severity Measure (GSM): Negatively Correlated with Learning Rate
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: GSM quantifies the magnitude of the grokking transition (delay and sharpness). It is negatively correlated with learning rate: higher LR reduces grokking severity because the model explores more of the loss landscape and discovers the generalising basin faster.
nodes.norm_label: grokking severity measure (gsm): negatively correlated with learning rate

nodes.label: Quadratic Network with Closed-Form LLC (λ = p·d(d+1)/4 or K·(d+p-1)/2)
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: For quadratic networks (f(x) = x^T W x) on modular arithmetic tasks, the LLC has closed-form expressions: λ = p·d(d+1)/4 for full dataset, λ = K·(d+p-1)/2 for under-parameterized case (K < (d+1)/2), λ(θ*) = ½ K_eff (d+p-1) via effective width K_eff in Stage-II.
nodes.norm_label: quadratic network with closed-form llc (λ = p·d(d+1)/4 or k·(d+p-1)/2)

nodes.label: SGLD for Posterior Sampling and LLC Estimation
nodes.author: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li
nodes.rationale: SGLD (Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics) is used to estimate LLC by sampling from the posterior near a training solution. The LLC is estimated from the slope of the expected loss under SGLD as a function of the number of SGLD steps times temperature, with log-linear dependence on SGLD learning rate.
nodes.norm_label: sgld for posterior sampling and llc estimation

nodes.label: LoRA Interference (Parameter-Data Interaction across Tasks Causing Merge Conflicts)
nodes.author: Haobo Zhang, Jiayu Zhou
nodes.rationale: LoRA interference arises when adapters trained on different tasks have overlapping subspaces in the weight update direction. When merged, this overlap causes destructive interference: task-specific updates cancel or corrupt each other, degrading merged model performance.
nodes.norm_label: lora interference (parameter-data interaction across tasks causing merge conflicts)

nodes.label: Orthogonal Subspace Constraint (Task 2 LoRA A2 orthogonal to Task 1 H1 subspace)
nodes.author: Haobo Zhang, Jiayu Zhou
nodes.rationale: OSRM constrains the LoRA A matrix of task 2 to lie in the null space of the H1 subspace (row space of task 1's LoRA A). This ensures the two adapters update orthogonal directions in weight space, eliminating destructive interference at merge time.
nodes.norm_label: orthogonal subspace constraint (task 2 lora a2 orthogonal to task 1 h1 subspace)

nodes.label: OSRM (Orthogonal Subspaces for Robust Model Merging) Method
nodes.author: Haobo Zhang, Jiayu Zhou
nodes.rationale: OSRM is a pre-finetuning subspace constraint method: before fine-tuning task 2, the LoRA subspace is projected to be orthogonal to task 1's subspace using sample covariance eigendecomposition. This reduces task interference and improves multi-task model merging quality.
nodes.norm_label: osrm (orthogonal subspaces for robust model merging) method

nodes.label: Subspace Overlap as Predictor of LoRA Merge Interference
nodes.author: Haobo Zhang, Jiayu Zhou
nodes.rationale: The paper shows that the degree of overlap between LoRA subspaces (measured by canonical angles between row spaces of A matrices) reliably predicts merge interference magnitude. High overlap → high interference → poor merge quality. OSRM minimises this overlap by construction.
nodes.norm_label: subspace overlap as predictor of lora merge interference

nodes.label: LoRA Model Merging (Multi-Task Integration without Retraining)
nodes.author: Haobo Zhang, Jiayu Zhou
nodes.rationale: LoRA model merging combines task-specific LoRA adapters into a single model without retraining, enabling multi-task capability. Quality depends heavily on adapter subspace design; OSRM is a principled approach to improve mergeability by construction via orthogonal constraints.
nodes.norm_label: lora model merging (multi-task integration without retraining)

nodes.label: Sample Covariance Eigendecomposition for LoRA Subspace Initialization
nodes.author: Haobo Zhang, Jiayu Zhou
nodes.rationale: OSRM uses eigendecomposition of sample covariance matrices computed from calibration data to identify the principal subspace directions of each task's LoRA adapter before fine-tuning. The orthogonal complement of a prior task's subspace is used to initialize the next task's LoRA A.
nodes.norm_label: sample covariance eigendecomposition for lora subspace initialization

nodes.label: Isotropic Model Merging via Spectral Skewness
nodes.description: Analyzes spectral skewness in Task Arithmetic merged models; proposes Iso-C and Iso-CTS algorithms to flatten singular value spectrum for improved multi-task merging
nodes.norm_label: isotropic model merging via spectral skewness

nodes.label: Learning on LoRAs: GL-Equivariant Processing of Low-Rank Weight Spaces
nodes.description: Formalizes GL(r)-equivariance symmetry in LoRA weight spaces; proposes GL-net architecture for equivariant processing of LoRA populations
nodes.norm_label: learning on loras: gl-equivariant processing of low-rank weight spaces

nodes.label: Reducing LoRA Interference via Orthogonal Subspace Initialization
nodes.description: Proposes OSRM: constraining LoRA A matrix to subspace orthogonal to out-of-task data distributions before fine-tuning to reduce cross-task interference in model merging
nodes.norm_label: reducing lora interference via orthogonal subspace initialization

nodes.label: LoRA Training in NTK Regime: No Spurious Local Minima
nodes.description: Proves LoRA training with prompt-based fine-tuning operates in NTK regime; establishes rank threshold above which all second-order stationary points are global minima
nodes.norm_label: lora training in ntk regime: no spurious local minima

nodes.label: LoRA Parameter Redundancy and Spectral Encoding (SeLoRA)
nodes.description: Analyzes rank and density redundancy in LoRA; proposes SeLoRA reparameterization via sparse inverse spectral transforms (DFT/wavelet)
nodes.norm_label: lora parameter redundancy and spectral encoding (selora)

nodes.label: Spectral Skewness
nodes.description: Non-uniform distribution of singular values in the merged task matrix from Task Arithmetic; few dominant singular values with long tail of small values. Controls effective rank k_M and subspace alignment ratio.

nodes.label: Isotropic Merging (Iso-C / Iso-CTS)
nodes.description: Model merging approach that flattens the singular value spectrum of the merged task matrix to uniform (isotropic) values. Iso-C rescales to average singular value; Iso-CTS adds task-specific orthogonal directions.

nodes.label: Iso-C Algorithm
nodes.description: Algorithm 1: sum task matrices, SVD, compute average singular value sigma_bar, reconstruct with isotropic spectrum. Basic isotropic merging variant.

nodes.label: Iso-CTS Algorithm
nodes.description: Algorithm 2: retain top-k common singular vectors, project out common subspace, compute task-specific SVDs, combine with orthogonalization via whitening, reconstruct with isotropic scaling. Achieves SOTA multi-task merging.

nodes.label: Subspace Alignment Ratio (SAR)
nodes.description: Metric quantifying overlap between subspaces of task matrix Delta_t and merged matrix Delta_M. SAR = ||Pi_{k_M,M} Delta_t||_F / ||Delta_t||_F. Strongly correlates (rho=0.94) with normalized accuracy improvement.

nodes.label: Task Matrix (Delta_t)
nodes.description: Layer-wise weight update Delta_t = theta_t - theta_0 computed as difference between fine-tuned and pre-trained weights. Core object of model merging analysis; analyzed via SVD.

nodes.label: Effective Rank (k_M)
nodes.description: Number of significant singular values in the merged task matrix; directly controlled by spectral skewness. Lower k_M means fewer directions capture variance, reducing subspace alignment with individual task matrices.

nodes.label: Task Arithmetic (TA)
nodes.description: Baseline model merging method: theta_TA = theta_0 + alpha * sum_t Delta_t. Produces skewed singular spectrum in the merged task matrix due to constructive/destructive interference.

nodes.label: TIES-Merging
nodes.description: Model merging method that resolves sign conflicts and prunes low-magnitude parameters before merging. Alternative to Task Arithmetic.

nodes.label: KnOTS
nodes.description: SVD-based LoRA merging method that concatenates low-rank matrices before merging. Used as evaluation protocol for LoRA-adapted model merging experiments.

nodes.label: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
nodes.description: Matrix factorization M = U*Sigma*V^T used throughout model merging, LoRA analysis, and weight space learning. Provides basis for spectral analysis of weight matrices.

nodes.label: Common Subspace
nodes.description: Shared singular directions across multiple task matrices; captured by top-k singular vectors of the merged task matrix Delta_M. Used in Iso-CTS to separate shared from task-specific representations.

nodes.label: Task-Specific Subspace
nodes.description: Per-task orthogonal directions added in Iso-CTS after projecting out common subspace. Preserves task-specific information not captured by the common subspace.

nodes.label: GL(r)-Equivariance/Invariance
nodes.description: LoRA weights (U,V) have symmetry under general linear group GL(r): U*R*R^{-1}*V^T = U*V^T for any invertible R. Any function learning on LoRAs must be invariant or equivariant to this symmetry.

nodes.label: Learning on LoRAs (LoL) Framework
nodes.description: Paradigm where LoRA weight matrices serve as input to ML models for predicting properties of fine-tuned models (e.g., downstream accuracy, aesthetic quality). Must handle GL(r) symmetry.

nodes.label: GL-net Architecture
nodes.description: Equivariant architecture for processing LoRA weights using GL-equivariant linear layers + GL-equivariant nonlinearities + invariant readout head. Provably GL-invariant.

nodes.label: GL-Equivariant Linear Layer
nodes.description: F_Linear(U_1,V_1,...,U_L,V_L) = (Phi_1*U_1, Psi_1*V_1,...). All linear GL-equivariant layers must have this form (Proposition 1). Acts separately on U and V matrices.

nodes.label: LoRA Symmetry Groups
nodes.description: LoRA has inner permutation symmetries (UP^T PV^T = UV^T) but NOT outer permutation symmetries. GL(r) is the full symmetry group; O(r) (orthogonal group) is a strict subgroup.

nodes.label: LoRA Population Manifold
nodes.description: The space of all LoRA fine-tuned models viewed as a manifold parameterized by (U, V) weight matrices. Quotiented by GL(r) symmetry; points on this manifold correspond to distinct fine-tuned behaviors.

nodes.label: Weight Space Learning
nodes.description: Learning directly from neural network weights as inputs; encompasses meta-learning, model editing, model merging prediction, and generation of weights. LoL is a specific instance for LoRA weights.

nodes.label: OSRM: Orthogonal Subspaces for Robust Model Merging
nodes.description: Method to constrain LoRA A matrix initialization to subspace orthogonal to out-of-task data distributions before fine-tuning. Minimizes cross-task interference in merged models.
nodes.norm_label: osrm: orthogonal subspaces for robust model merging

nodes.label: Orthogonal Subspace Initialization
nodes.description: Analytical solution for OSRM: initialize LoRA A as the last r eigenvectors (smallest eigenvalues) of the sample covariance matrix S = (1/(k-1))*H^T*H of latent features.

nodes.label: Data-Parameter Interaction
nodes.description: Interplay between latent features H and LoRA parameter updates BA. Minimizing ||A_2*H_1^T||_F reduces cross-task interference by ensuring task 2's LoRA A does not activate task 1's feature directions.

nodes.label: Task Interference
nodes.description: When merging multiple LoRA fine-tuned models, one task's parameter updates degrade performance on other tasks. Caused by non-orthogonal subspace overlap between task-specific LoRA A matrices and other tasks' feature distributions.

nodes.label: Orthogonal Procrustes Problem
nodes.description: Used in OSRM to verify LoRA A matrix remains close to its orthogonal initialization after fine-tuning. D = min_Omega ||Omega*A^{ft} - A^{init}||_F. Change found to be ≤14% empirically.

nodes.label: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) Regime
nodes.description: Linearized training dynamics where network change is approximated by first-order Taylor expansion. LoRA training with prompt-based fine-tuning empirically operates in NTK regime; enables theoretical guarantees.

nodes.label: Spurious Local Minima
nodes.description: Local minima that are not global minima in the optimization landscape. Eliminated in LoRA NTK setting when rank r satisfies r(r+1)/2 > KN (Theorem 4.1). All SOSPs become global minima above this threshold.

nodes.label: Rank Threshold for No Spurious Minima
nodes.description: Sufficient rank condition r >= sqrt(N) for no spurious local minima in LoRA NTK regime. Derived from r(r+1)/2 > KN where K is number of classes and N is number of training samples.
nodes.norm_label: rank threshold for no spurious minima

nodes.label: Second-Order Stationary Points (SOSPs)
nodes.description: Points where gradient is zero and Hessian is positive semi-definite. Shown to be global minima in LoRA NTK regime above rank threshold (Theorem 4.1). Key concept in non-convex optimization theory.

nodes.label: Nuclear Norm Regularization
nodes.description: Equivalent to weight decay on LoRA factor matrices via Burer-Monteiro connection. Minimizing L + (lambda/2)||u||^2 + (lambda/2)||v||^2 is equivalent to minimizing L_lambda + lambda*||delta||_* (nuclear norm).

nodes.label: Rademacher Complexity
nodes.description: Statistical measure used to derive generalization bounds for low-rank LoRA solutions. Theorem 5.1 bounds generalization error in terms of nuclear norm of optimal solution and Rademacher complexity.

nodes.label: Burer-Monteiro Factorization
nodes.description: Matrix factorization approach delta = u*v^T connecting LoRA parameterization to nuclear norm regularization. Low-rank factorization that enables theoretical analysis of LoRA optimization landscape.

nodes.label: LoRA Adaptation
nodes.description: Low-rank adaptation method: W' = W_0 + B*A where B in R^{m x r}, A in R^{r x n}, r << min(m,n). Parameter-efficient fine-tuning paradigm that introduces low-rank structure into weight updates.

nodes.label: Parameter Redundancy in LoRA
nodes.description: Two types of redundancy in LoRA: (1) rank redundancy - some ranks can be reduced without performance loss; (2) density redundancy - optimizing only sparse subset of parameters preserves expressive power.

nodes.label: SeLoRA: Spectral-encoding Low-Rank Adaptation
nodes.description: Reparameterizes LoRA adaptation matrices as spatial recovery of sparse spectral components via inverse spectral transforms. W' = W_0 + T(F_B)*T(F_A) with sparse spectral matrices F_A, F_B.

nodes.label: Fourier Encoding in SeLoRA (SeLoRA_F)
nodes.description: Uses 2D inverse DFT to map sparse spectral matrix F_A to spatial adaptation matrix A_tilde. A_tilde(j,k) = Re[F^{-1}(F_A)] = Re[sum_{u,v} F_A(u,v)*e^{i2pi(uj/r + vk/d)}].

nodes.label: Wavelet Encoding in SeLoRA (SeLoRA_W)
nodes.description: Uses 2D inverse wavelet transform for more stable, localized spectral representation. Default uses 2D inverse Haar wavelet; alternatives: Daubechies-4, Biorthogonal, Coiflets.

nodes.label: Spectral Encoding
nodes.description: General approach of learning in frequency/spectral domain rather than spatial domain. Sparse spectral matrix F_A with only floor((1-eta)*r*d) learnable entries implicitly encodes a dense spatial adaptation matrix.

nodes.label: Amplification Factor (AF) / Reverse AF
nodes.description: AF = ||DeltaW||_F / ||U_r^T*W*V_r||_F measures amplification of top-r W features. RAF = ||DeltaW||_F / ||U_{d-r}^T*W*V_{d-r}||_F measures amplification of bottom features. SeLoRA reduces RAF (0.04 vs 0.17 for LoRA).

nodes.label: Singular Value Spectrum
nodes.description: Distribution of singular values of a weight matrix or task matrix. Non-uniform (skewed) spectrum leads to effective rank reduction in merged models. Core diagnostic tool for model merging quality.

nodes.label: Optimal LoRA Rank
nodes.description: Minimum rank r sufficient for no spurious local minima: r >= sqrt(N). Also studied in parameter redundancy context: optimal rank for best performance-efficiency tradeoff.

nodes.label: Sample Covariance of Latent Features
nodes.description: S = (1/(k-1))*H^T*H computed from latent features H of out-of-task data. Eigenvectors define the subspace directions; OSRM initializes LoRA A to last r eigenvectors (smallest eigenvalue directions).

nodes.label: Low-Rank Solution Existence Theorem
nodes.description: Theorem 3.1: A low-rank LoRA solution exists with rank r satisfying r(r+1)/2 <= KN. Establishes fundamental existence result before proving optimization landscape properties.

nodes.label: ViT Models (B/32, B/16, L/14)
nodes.description: Vision Transformer architectures used as base models for isotropic merging experiments. Evaluated on 8/14/20-task vision benchmarks.

nodes.label: RoBERTa Models
nodes.description: RoBERTa-large used in OSRM experiments (rank=8, alpha=16, query+value only); RoBERTa-base used in NTK regime experiments (N=32 samples, SST-2/QNLI/CR/QQP/Subj tasks).

nodes.label: LLaMA Models (2-7B, 3-8B)
nodes.description: LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B used in SeLoRA experiments. Rank r=32, alpha=64. +2.0 avg accuracy on commonsense reasoning.
